title: I built an 8-player co-op incremental game with AI—and finished the Steam page, build review, and trailer in one day
author: Fun_Examination8599
selftext:
I wanted to share my AI-assisted game development project: **Sir, We Have 100 Million Rocks!**

In a single day, I completed the Steam store page, got through the build review, and finished the trailer. It’s now getting ready for release!

It’s an **8-player co-op cleanup incremental game**, except the mess you’re cleaning up is an absurd amount of rocks.

The loop is simple:

* Smash rocks and collect resources.
* Buy goblins to help with the mining.
* Lay rails to transport what you collect.
* Upgrade your operation, then tackle even more rocks.

The main hook is that **mining feels like a hack-and-slash game**. Instead of slowly chipping away at one rock at a time, you unleash flashy abilities across huge fields of them. Meteors, chain lightning, black holes—the goal is to make breaking rocks feel ridiculously satisfying.

You can play solo or bring up to seven friends to help turn the chaos into a growing mining operation.

I used generative AI throughout development, including code, visuals, audio, and marketing materials. Seeing the game, store page, and trailer come together this quickly has been a pretty wild experience.

Here’s the Steam page  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5637340/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5637340/)



I’d love some honest feedback: **does the “hack-and-slash mining” idea come across clearly from the trailer?**
